extracted.intended_audience: university and research-institute communications officers, science communicators, and scholars of science communication
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate or craft institutional science press releases for likelihood of media pickup and direct public readership, emphasizing institutional credibility, multimedia readiness, embargo discipline, and cross-channel coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional-trust signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release prominently identify the issuing institution and use the institution's standard branding/letterhead/template? Editors lean on institutional reputation as a quality proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Autzen argues that pickup-rate is partly a function of the issuing institution's perceived trustworthiness, not just the text. Use consistent institutional branding and clearly state the institution to convey trustworthiness to thin newsroom editors who use reputation as a shortcut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-authority alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the named scientist a co-author on the cited paper and identified by full title at the issuing institution? Releases naming someone other than a paper author lose institutional credibility weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the quoted or named expert is actually an author on the research and is given full institutional title/affiliation to maintain credibility; avoid naming external commentators in ways that dilute institutional authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are images, video, and B-roll embedded with usage rights cleared, captioned, and high-resolution? Multimedia is a competitive frontier among universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ready-to-use assets (high-res images, captioned video/B-roll) with clear usage rights and captions so newsrooms can copy/paste materials without clearance delays; production quality (visuals, video) now affects pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release respect the journal's embargo and clearly state the embargo time / lift time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State embargo details explicitly and coordinate timing precisely; institutions that manage embargoes reliably gain favor with journalists and peer institutions during competitive release windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct-publication path
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release contain a link to the open-access version of the paper or a media DOI?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include direct links to the paper (preferably open-access) or a media DOI so journalists and public readers can immediately access the source; this supports both journalist verification and public readership when the release is consumed as a standalone document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuing institution as publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release recognize that the public will read the release on the institution's news site directly, not through a journalist? The lead and structure should be readable as standalone public communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the lead and overall structure so the release functions as a public-facing article the institution will stand behind; avoid treating it solely as a journalist-facing brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-channel coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the release coordinated with the institution's social-media post, faculty page update, and open-day calendar so each channel reinforces the others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan simultaneous updates across social media, faculty pages, event calendars, and other institutional channels to amplify reach and present a coherent narrative; coordination increases effectiveness of the release as a publishing product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable-institution scan
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release avoid duplicating a competing institution's release on the same week? Crowding reduces pickup likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor competing institutions' schedules and avoid releasing similar announcements concurrently; crowding effects mean even high-quality releases can be overlooked if multiple institutions push comparable items at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-document standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release contain nothing the institution would not be comfortable defending as its own published statement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet claims and language against what the institution would stand behind publicly; treat the release as an official published statement and avoid speculative or indefensible phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation-loss hedge
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a release will likely be translated into other languages by international wires, does the original release avoid idioms that translate poorly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, literal language and avoid culture-specific idioms so translations retain intended meaning; consider international distribution when choosing phrasing and examples.
